breaks.why: Replacing $wp_filter wholesale: the global becomes a plain PHP array, no longer the proxy over the Rust hook store, which does not see it.
Replacing $wp_filter wholesale (with the result of build_preinitialized_hooks): the Rust hook store does not see it. Hooks set before the request's PHP code runs are imported.
$wp_filter holds only WP_Hook objects: assigning anything else to $wp_filter[$name] throws a TypeError.

limits.what: Passing $wp_filter, $wp_actions or $wp_filters to an array function (array_keys, array_key_exists, in_array, array_pop, ...)
limits.why: They are proxy objects over the Rust hook store: reading, indexing, isset, iterating, counting and appending work as in WordPress; array functions throw a TypeError. $wp_current_filter is a real array and is not affected.
